Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. The scan supplied is complete: cover page and questions 1 to 8 (4 pages), eight questions all compulsory; the marks printed in the margin add up to 13 for each question.
enonce_intro_markdown: A truck of mass $7500\ \mathrm{kg}$ is moving with constant speed $v\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ down a straight road inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = \tfrac{1}{25}$. The resistance to the motion of the truck is of magnitude $4800\ \mathrm{N}$. The engine of the truck is working at a constant rate of $54\ \mathrm{kW}$. (Take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.)
incertitudes: Question 7 : « Take g as 10 ms^-2 » est imprimé ; valeur retenue g = 10 m s^-2.

Question 7 (c) : DONNEES IMPRIMEES INCOHERENTES. Moteur coupé à 5 m/s, avec résistance 4800 N et composante du poids 3000 N, la décélération vaut 7800/7500 = 1,04 m/s^2 : arrêt après 4,81 s et distance 625/52 = 12,0 m. Or le sujet dit « it comes to rest after 40 seconds » : avec décélération uniforme de 5 m/s à 0 en 40 s, la distance est 100 m. Le corrigé donne 100 m (utilise les données explicites de (c)) et signale l'incohérence et la valeur 12,0 m. L'énoncé de (c) rappelle les données communes de la question pour être autonome.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Positive direction down the slope. Forces along the slope on the truck: the driving force $D$ of the engine (down the slope, in the direction of motion), the component of the weight $mg\sin\theta$ (down the slope), and the resistance $4800\ \mathrm{N}$ (up the slope, opposing the motion). The speed is constant, so the acceleration is zero. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ (printed).

$$mg\sin\theta = 7500\times 10\times\tfrac{1}{25} = 3000\ \mathrm{N}$$

$$D + 3000 - 4800 = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; D = 1800\ \mathrm{N}$$

**Power $=$ driving force $\times$ speed:**

$$54\,000 = 1800\,v \;\Rightarrow\; v = 30$$

**$v = 30\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.**
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance

questions.enonce_markdown: The truck now moves up the same straight road. Given that the truck is working at the same rate and that the resistance to its motion remains unchanged, find the acceleration of the truck at the instant when it is moving with speed $5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Positive direction up the slope. At speed $5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ the driving force is

$$D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{54\,000}{5} = 10\,800\ \mathrm{N}$$

Forces opposing the motion (down the slope): the resistance $4800\ \mathrm{N}$ and the weight component $mg\sin\theta = 3000\ \mathrm{N}$ (with $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, printed).

**Newton's second law along the slope:**

$$10\,800 - 4800 - 3000 = 7500\,a \;\Rightarrow\; a = \frac{3000}{7500} = 0.4$$

**The acceleration is $0.4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ up the slope.**
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance

questions.enonce_markdown: A truck of mass $7500\ \mathrm{kg}$ moves up a straight road inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = \tfrac{1}{25}$; the resistance to its motion has magnitude $4800\ \mathrm{N}$. The engine of the truck is switched off when its speed is $5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and it comes to rest after $40$ seconds. Find the distance covered by the truck before it comes to momentary rest. (Take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** After the engine is switched off, the only forces along the slope are the resistance and the weight component, both constant and both down the slope. The truck therefore decelerates uniformly, so the constant-acceleration formulae apply. Initial speed $u = 5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, final speed $0$, time $40\ \mathrm{s}$ (as printed).

**Distance using the printed data** (average speed $\times$ time):

$$s = \frac{u + 0}{2}\times t = \frac{5 + 0}{2}\times 40 = 100\ \mathrm{m}$$

(The deceleration implied is $\tfrac{5}{40} = 0.125\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.)

**Consistency check with the forces of parts (a) and (b).** With the engine off, $7500\,a = 4800 + 3000 = 7800$, so the deceleration would be $\tfrac{7800}{7500} = 1.04\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, and the truck would stop after $\tfrac{5}{1.04} \approx 4.81\ \mathrm{s}$, having travelled $\tfrac{5^{2}}{2\times 1.04} = \tfrac{625}{52} \approx 12.0\ \mathrm{m}$. This contradicts the printed $40\ \mathrm{s}$: the data of the question are not consistent with each other.

**Answer using the stated data (rest after $40\ \mathrm{s}$): $100\ \mathrm{m}$.** (If the time of $40\ \mathrm{s}$ is ignored and the forces of the question are used, the distance would be $\approx 12.0\ \mathrm{m}$, see the note above.)
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance
